title: Grove has no emergency response protocol at either ecosystem or Agent scope while operating live allocations
content:
Two adjacent sections define the same gap at two scopes. A.6.1.1.2.3.1.2 covers "Grove's emergency response protocol in situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem" and states: "This protocol **will be specified in a future iteration** of the Grove Artifact." A.6.1.1.2.3.1.3 covers situations "solely impacting Grove versus the broader Sky Ecosystem" and says the same.

Set against the rest of the Artifact, the omission stands out. Grove maintains well over a dozen Active Instances spanning seven networks, with individual daily inflow allowances up to 50,000,000 and an asset-level USDG ceiling of 100 million USDS. Each Instance is specified to the level of individual RateLimitID hashes and tick bounds. The document is extremely precise about steady-state operation and silent about failure.

The two scopes matter separately, and their pairing shows the omission is structural rather than an oversight of one case. An ecosystem-wide event raises questions of coordination and precedence — who decides, and how Grove's actions compose with other Agents'. A Grove-only event raises questions of unilateral authority — what Grove may do without waiting for governance. Neither is answered.

The gap compounds specific findings elsewhere in the Artifact. Unlimited outflow limits are justified partly by the need for a fast exit, and timelocked counterparty roles give Grove a warning window whose value depends entirely on acting within it. Both presuppose someone empowered to act quickly under pressure. The provision that would establish who that is, and what they may do, is the one deferred.

To the Artifact's credit, the gap is declared in the place where the answer belongs rather than left blank — the same forward-reference convention used for missing RateLimitIDs. It remains the most consequential deferral in the document.
description: Both A.6.1.1.2.3.1.2 and A.6.1.1.2.3.1.3 defer their protocols to a future iteration, leaving conduits with hundreds of millions in authorized daily inflow without a documented crisis procedure.
